name: MS-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+11 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent party
Bennie Thompson holds a massive fundraising and cash-on-hand edge over Ron Eller
Prediction markets price Thompson near 97% to win
No competitive polling or expert ratings, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Thompson: a D+11 district, a long-tenured incumbent seeking renomination and reelection, and a challenger who has raised under $50,000 against more than $1.4 million in cash on hand. Markets price the race at roughly 97% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any sign of outside spending against Thompson or an unexpectedly competitive primary would be the main signal that this seat is less secure than it appears.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mississippi's 2nd District is a solidly Democratic seat in western Mississippi, anchored by Jackson and the Delta, with a partisan lean of about D+11. Bennie Thompson, a longtime incumbent, is running for another term and has more than $1.4 million on hand after raising roughly $770,000 this cycle.

Republican Ron Eller has raised only about $45,000 and faces a steep financial and structural disadvantage, with no outside spending reported on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Thompson about a 97% chance of winning. The district's lean, incumbency, and money gap all point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
